blocks.text: This opening contents page for Volume I gathers the foreword, preface, introduction, the early Guru-centred episodes, and the first Banda Bahadur arc into one browsable editorial outline.
Front matter and opening interpretive essays
Foreword; Preface; A Significant Source of Sikh History; Introduction.
Origins, Guru Nanak, and the udasi journeys

The contents then move through the Origin of the Khalsa, the Second Episode, the First Sikh Guni, the Dialogue Between Baba Nanak and Kaliyuga, and the udasi journeys to the south, east, west, and north.
Imperial pressure and the rise of Guru Gobind Singh

A later cluster highlights the Delhi Emperor, Emperor Karon, the Lineage of the Sikh Gurus, Aurangzeb's Tyranny, the Tenth Sikh Guru, another linked episode, the Creation of the Khalsa Panth, and the Expansion of the Khalsa Panth.
Anandpur, sacrifice, and the road south

The outline continues through Anandpur Sahib, the Battle at Anandpur Sahib, the Sacrifice of the Elder Sahibzadas, Machhiwara, Kangar, Tapa, and Dina villages, the Jaal Piloo forest, Muktsar Sahib, Sabo Talwandi, Rain in the Malwa Region, and Guru Gobind Singh's Movement to the South.

The page closes by listing the First Episode About Banda Bahadur, the Second Episode About Banda Bahadur, Guru Gobind Singh's Encounter with Banda, the Prayer of the Khalsa, and Banda Singh's Faith in the Guru.
